title: Epic: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (gateway, routing, runtime signals, observability)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Reliability Program: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
description:
Why this epic exists
Hosted API traffic is bursty and highly variable (prompt lengths, streaming, customer spikes). When capacity or dependencies are saturated we currently see tail latency blowups, ambiguous timeouts/5xx, and noisy-neighbor effects. This epic delivers explicit overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) across the request path so we degrade safely and predictably.

Goals (what “done” means)
- Prevent overload cascades by rejecting or degrading traffic early and consistently.
- Customer-facing errors have stable semantics (status + code + retry guidance + correlation id) vs random 5xx/timeouts.
- Tenant/tier aware behavior (self-serve vs enterprise Hosted vs Dedicated-backed) with per-route/model controls.
- Observability and operability: dashboards, alerts, runbooks; tuning loop and rollout guardrails.
- Measurable improvements under bursts: reduced p95/p99, reduced timeout rates, lower saturation-related incidents.

Non-goals (for this epic)
- Pricing/credits policy changes (only usage enforcement hooks needed to support admission decisions).
- Full cross-cloud brokering beyond existing routing primitives.
- Major SDK surface redesign (docs + additive error handling only).

High-level architecture (layering)
- Gateway/control plane: admission control + circuit breaker evaluation + consistent error payloads.
- Smart routing: overload-aware fallback to compatible model/region when configured; loop prevention.
- Serving runtime: exports bounded-cardinality saturation signals (queue depth, token/sec saturation, KV/memory pressure proxies) and enforces local backpressure.
- Observability: shed rate, breaker open rate, queue depth, saturation indicators, downstream health signals; SLO classification rules.

Work breakdown (tracked as child issues)
1) Error taxonomy + payload standardization
- ENG-4822 Define overload error codes/payloads and implement across gateway + downstream mappings.
- Alignment with ADR-014 (status mapping, Retry-After semantics, additive fields).

2) Gateway admission control + breaker framework
- ENG-4823 Implement middleware for admission (token bucket + concurrency caps) with policy engine integration and metrics.
- Ensure consistent correlation IDs and no retry storms.

3) Smart routing hooks for overload + fallback
- ENG-4824 Add routing behavior when breaker open: optional fallback model/region w/ bounded retries + loop prevention.
- Safety constraints: tenant policy must explicitly allow; do not silently change model without config.

4) Runtime saturation signals + backpressure integration
- ENG-4825 Export saturation signals from runtime with aggregation to keep metric cardinality bounded.
- Ensure signals are stable enough to drive policy without oscillations.

5) Dashboards, alerts, and oncall operationalization
- ENG-4826 Ship dashboards + alert rules with runbook links; tune initial thresholds.
- Update SLO tooling classification rules (ties to hosted availability reporting).

6) Validation / game day and docs
- ENG-4830 Run overload simulation game day and capture follow-ups.
- ENG-4832 Update SDK/docs guidance for Retry-After + exponential backoff + jitter + idempotency notes.

Milestones + rollout plan
Phase 0 (Weeks 1–2): Requirements + customer-facing semantics
- Deliverables: ADR-014 + ADR-015 reviewed; payload shape finalized; initial SLO classification approach agreed.
- Gate: PM sign-off on customer-visible language and Support/CS readiness plan.

Phase 1 (Weeks 3–6): Implementation + dark launch
- Gateway admission path wired; runtime signals exported; routing fallback behind flag.
- Dark launch metrics: emit “would_shed” decisions without rejecting to baseline false positives.
- Gate: false-positive rate below agreed threshold; no material added latency in gateway.

Phase 2 (Weeks 7–9): Canary
- Canary in one region + subset of tenants; progressive enablement.
- Tune thresholds; validate no retry storms; validate that errors are actionable.
- Gate: p99 latency does not regress; timeout rate drops during synthetic burst tests.

Phase 3 (Weeks 10–12): GA + operationalization
- Roll out to remaining regions; finalize runbooks + paging; post-launch review.
- Gate: oncall playbook validated; Support macros/docs live; rollback triggers documented.

Success metrics (initial)
- Under burst: lower p95/p99 latency and fewer request timeouts.
- Reduced overload-related incident count/severity and improved MTTR.
- Shed rate/breaker opens are visible and explainable; customers receive stable 429/503 + Retry-After guidance rather than ambiguous 5xx.

Key risks / open questions
- Oscillation/feedback loops: avoid using unstable signals directly; smoothing + hysteresis required.
- Retry storms: must set Retry-After consistently and document client behavior.
- Policy safety: guardrails to prevent tenants from misconfiguring fallbacks/thresholds in ways that cause loops or silent quality regressions.
- Cardinality: saturation metrics must remain bounded; avoid per-request/per-prompt dimensions.

Updates
- 2025-11-03 (PM/Eng): Error taxonomy approved pending final Retry-After defaults and status page wording alignment.
- 2025-11-18 (SRE): Canary go/no-go checklist drafted; monitoring gates defined (shed rate, open rate, p99, timeouts).
- 2025-12-05 (Eng): Gateway admission and error payloads in review; runtime queue depth metrics merged behind aggregation. Next: hook routing fallback into breaker-open path and run burst scenario in perf-canary before enabling canary in us-east.

Notes for oncall/readiness
- Rollout must include fast rollback toggles at gateway + routing layers.
- Any partial rollout requires Support/CS macro updates and a canonical explanation of 503 overload vs 5xx failure.
- All breakers/load shedding must emit structured reason codes for post-incident analysis (and to avoid “unknown overload” buckets).
